paragraphs.text: Thus the wicked derided the prophets as though they preached only errors, and therefore gave themselves still to their pleasures.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: We will not be pulled out of Jerusalem, till the hour of our death comes, as the flesh is not taken out of the caldron until it is boiled.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Contrary to their vain confidence he shows in what sense the city is the caldron: that is, because of the dead bodies that have been murdered in it, and so lit as flesh in the caldron.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: It seems that this noble man died of some terrible death, and therefore the prophet feared some strange judgment of God toward the rest of the people.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: They that remained at Jerusalem thus reproached them that were gone into captivity as though they were cast off and forsaken by God.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: They will be yet a little church: showing that the Lord will ever have some to call on his Name, whom he will preserve and restore, though they are for a time afflicted.
